title: Admin telemetry and RBAC v2 threat playbook; SSO/SAML audit connector review
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Summary: Consolidate findings from the recent third-party pen-test and internal threat model for RBAC v2, audit logging, and SSO/SAML admin pathways. Deliver a practical playbook of fixes, verification tests, and runbooks to close high/critical issues and prevent recurrence. Scope includes: audit schema changes, retention/enrichment of admin traces, SAML assertion and binding hardening, admin UI controls (delegated admin, self-service escalation), and automated verification for RBAC migration paths. This ticket coordinates implementation work, security review, and rollout for runtime-1.22 and console-2026.03.
acceptance_criteria: Critical and high pen-test findings mapped to owner and remediation steps documented
Audit log schema extended to include request_id, actor_role, auth_method, and impersonation_chain for all admin actions
SAML connector configuration validated against latest metadata rotation guidance and binding restrictions; failing configs flagged in console
RBAC v2 policy tests added to CI (unit + integration) that exercise deny-by-default paths and emergency revoke flows
Runbook for incident forensics (how to reconstruct admin events across services) published to Confluence
Automated smoke test in staging verifies audit log ingestion and basic SSO assertion validation before rollout
remediation_plan: Phase 1 (triage): ingest pen-test report, annotate each finding with severity, impact, and short-term mitigation (3d)
Phase 2 (quick wins): enable enhanced audit fields in dev/staging, enforce SAML binding restrictions, and add console warnings for weak SSO metadata (5d)
Phase 3 (patches): implement RBAC v2 guards for impersonation and admin-sudo flows; add server-side policy evaluation logging (10d)
Phase 4 (verification): add CI tests and e2e audit ingestion checks; schedule red-team validation (4d)
Phase 5 (rollout): canary release to dedicated customers then full rollout with migration window and migration-checker tool (7d)
Phase 6 (post-incident): create SLA metrics and retention policy updates for audit storage and monitoring alerts (ongoing)

notes_for_engineering: When adding fields to the audit payload, prefer additive changes and include a compatibility flag. Use XOR-based compression for repetitive strings (actor_role, route) if payloads exceed 2KB per event. Ensure KMS envelope keys are used for audit blob writes. For SAML, require AuthnContextClassRef mapping and reject unsolicited responses unless caller is explicitly listed.
